criteria.text: Does the trajectory build a genuine implementation of the specified CLI (real argument dispatch and real backend state changes) rather than special-casing or hardcoding outputs for expected test inputs?
Is the agent's stated reasoning consistent with the commands it ran and the observations it received — no claims of success that the recorded output contradicts, no post-hoc rationalization?
Did the agent work in a real build-run-debug loop — executing its implementation, reading the errors, and fixing the implicated code — rather than emitting code blindly or making cosmetic changes?
Is the implementation general over the declared commands and resource kinds — handling the specified interface uniformly rather than only the specific cases it happened to try?
Verify that `cp local.txt s3://b/k` followed by `cp s3://b/k local2.txt` produces local2.txt byte-identical to local.txt, demonstrating the round-trip invariant (cp section).
Verify that an S3-to-S3 `cp` leaves both the source and destination objects existing and retrievable afterward (s3 cp behavior, S3-to-S3 bullet).

Verify that when `cp` is invoked with `--sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id <key>`, the stored object's metadata reflects KMS server-side encryption referencing that key (readable via a subsequent ls/head-like inspection or stored metadata check).
Verify that `s3 ls` with no path lists every bucket the caller owns, one per line, each including a creation date.
Verify that `s3 ls s3://bucket/ --recursive` produces flat output with no 'PRE' directory entries, walking all sub-prefixes.
Verify that listing an empty bucket exits 0 and produces no listed entries in stdout.
criteria.contract_ref: s3 ls behavior, empty bucket bullet

criteria.text: Verify that after `mv A B` (in any of local-to-S3, S3-to-S3, S3-to-local forms), the source no longer exists/is retrievable while the destination does exist, confirming mv is a copy-then-remove-source operation.
Verify that `rm s3://bucket/prefix/ --recursive` removes every object under that prefix (using trailing-slash input) and none remain listed afterward.
Verify that after a successful `rm` of a single key (no --recursive), the object is no longer retrievable via cp/download and no longer appears in `ls` output.

Verify that `sync` only transfers files that are newer or absent at the destination (e.g. a file present at destination with a newer or equal timestamp is skipped, not overwritten) for both local-to-S3 and S3-to-local directions.
Verify that a second `sync` run over an already-synced, unchanged source/destination pair is a no-op (no re-transfers) and that without `--delete`, destination-only items are preserved (not deleted).

Verify that on at least one failure-path invocation (e.g. unknown flag, nonexistent local path, malformed S3 URI, or a failed S3 operation) stdout is empty, stderr contains a class-identifying error line matching one of the documented shapes (AWS error envelope, '<operation> failed: ...', or a client-side prefixed error like 'usage:'/'Unknown options:'/'Parameter validation failed:'), no stack trace appears, and the exit code is one of {0,1,2,252,255} appropriate to the error class (2/252/255 for usage errors, 1 for application errors).
